hints: Express the volume of the cuboid as $V = x^2(10 - x) = 10x^2 - x^3$ and find $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}x}$.
Substitute $t = \dfrac{1}{10}, x = \dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = -\dfrac{20}{37}$ to find the proportionality constant $k = \dfrac{1}{2}$.
walkthrough:
Write the volume of the cuboid with square base side $x$ and height $10 - x$:
$$V = x^2(10 - x) = 10x^2 - x^3$$

State the rate equation for volume, given that $V$ decreases at a rate inversely proportional to $t$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t} = -\dfrac{k}{t} \quad (k > 0)$$

Apply the chain rule relating the derivatives:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}x} \cdot \dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}$$
$$-\dfrac{k}{t} = (20x - 3x^2)\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = -\dfrac{k}{t(20x - 3x^2)}$$

Substitute the given conditions $t = \dfrac{1}{10}$, $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$, and $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = -\dfrac{20}{37}$:
$$20x - 3x^2 = 20\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) - 3\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) = 10 - \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{37}{4}$$
$$t(20x - 3x^2) = \left(\dfrac{1}{10}\right)\left(\dfrac{37}{4}\right) = \dfrac{37}{40}$$
$$-\dfrac{20}{37} = -\dfrac{k}{\dfrac{37}{40}} = -\dfrac{40k}{37}$$
$$40k = 20 \implies k = \dfrac{20}{40} = \dfrac{1}{2}$$

ai_rubric.Differential-Equation Modelling: States $dV/dt = -k/t$ (B1). Obtains $dV/dx = 20x - 3x^2$ (B1). Uses chain rule $dV/dt = (dV/dx)(dx/dt)$ (M1). Substitutes initial values to find $k = 1/2$ (A1). Concludes with given differential equation (A1).

skill_tags: Applying Initial Conditions to Differential Equations

hints: Separate variables in $(20x - 3x^2)\,\mathrm{d}x = -\dfrac{1}{2t}\,\mathrm{d}t$ and integrate both sides.
Evaluate the constant of integration using $t = \dfrac{1}{10}$ when $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$.
Exponentiate to obtain an explicit expression for $t$ in terms of $x$.
walkthrough:
Separate variables in the differential equation:
$$(20x - 3x^2)\,\mathrm{d}x = -\dfrac{1}{2t}\,\mathrm{d}t$$
Multiply through by $2$:
$$(40x - 6x^2)\,\mathrm{d}x = -\dfrac{1}{t}\,\mathrm{d}t$$

Determine constant $C$ using the initial condition $t = \dfrac{1}{10}$ when $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$:
$$20\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) - 2\left(\dfrac{1}{8}\right) = -\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{10}\right) + C$$
$$5 - \dfrac{1}{4} = -(-\ln 10) + C$$
$$\dfrac{19}{4} = \ln 10 + C \implies C = \dfrac{19}{4} - \ln 10$$

Substitute $C$ back into the integrated equation:
$$20x^2 - 2x^3 = -\ln t + \dfrac{19}{4} - \ln 10$$

Exponentiate both sides with base $\mathrm{e}$ to solve for $t$:
$$10t = \mathrm{e}^{2x^3 - 20x^2 + \frac{19}{4}}$$
$$t = \dfrac{1}{10}\mathrm{e}^{2x^3 - 20x^2 + \frac{19}{4}}$$

ai_rubric.Applying Initial Conditions to Different: Separates variables correctly (B1). Integrates polynomial side to $20x^2 - 2x^3$ (or $10x^2 - x^3$) (B1). Integrates $t$ side to $-\ln t$ (or $-\frac{1}{2}\ln t$) (B1). Uses initial condition to evaluate constant (M1). Obtains correct logarithmic relation (A1). Obtains $t = \frac{1}{10}e^{2x^3 - 20x^2 + 19/4}$ (A1).
